question: Does high apparent ring healing arise from repeated native adjacency and energy-qualified ordinary M6 pair-formation lottery, rather than a structure-aware repair mechanism?

sample.native_ring: exact existing unchanged M7.11 scan_first_native_aged_ring(seed), original M6.4 simple 4/6/8 rings, >=20 uninterrupted same original material edge snapshots, first eligible >=120, by tick600, all noneligible seeds retained
sample.unit: one numeric seed-world, one first naturally aged ring per seed. Native pair events are NOT independent units

intervention.method: Clone frozen first natural aged ring, cut lexicographically first native bond and refund exact stored bond energy via ORIGINAL M7.11 excise_refund, no extra dissipation or RNG, one arm only. Resume native M6 steps and unchanged original M7.3 bond_only poststep conduction 120 ticks.
intervention.endpoint: Actual native original M6 FORM event of exact first cut pair before any other original ring edge actually breaks, including same-tick break events
intervention.instrumentation: A no-side-effect observer wraps alife.chemistry._candidate_pairs ONLY for the duration of each native World.advance(1), records each true target pair yielded by original native candidate generator at the exact formation stage; no extra RNG or modified candidates. Restore original function in finally, compare original world hash and RNG across shadow replay of first eligible source in each shard.
intervention.separation: At every pre-formation tick record whether target endpoints remain von-Neumann adjacent and each still has another original surviving ring bond; two endpoints of an opened unbranched ring remain anchored by surviving edges until a real original break. Log actual candidate counts, initial target species/energy/valence eligibility, and native formation events, never infer events just from final snapshots.
intervention.frozen_single_step: At exact original post-cut state run 32 preregistered M7.8 pair-keyed single formation sweeps on clones with same geometry/energy, for mechanistic cross-check; these are NOT independent native worlds, NOT native future trajectory, and should never replace native reclosure result.

preregistered_decisions.primary_exposure_mechanism: >=40 eligible native ring source worlds, >=100 observed target original pair native candidate events across selected worlds before target first FORM or other-original-edge break, >=95% of ALL actual exact target early native FORM events must have a recorded TRUE _candidate_pairs target event in SAME native step. This is a MECHANISTIC CORRECTNESS/COVERAGE gate (almost guaranteed by correct native physics), not statistical discovery or independent evidence of active repair. If fails report implementation/anomaly; if passes merely confirms no extra hidden repair route.
preregistered_decisions.secondary_native_probability: Compute number of actual FIRST native target FORM successes per total target-pair candidate opportunity events before first target FORM or other edge break. Report empirical event ratio and native unmodified formation_probability (0.05), 95% Wilson interval. Preregister simple descriptive model adequacy band 0.03..0.07 if >=100 attempts; NOT a statistical test for adaptive repair because time-censoring and native coupled RNG streams make IID assumptions approximate. No posthoc threshold change.
preregistered_decisions.geometry: Report fraction of at-risk ticks with adjacency, anchored endpoints, energy-eligible target and native candidate; fraction where only energy/valence blocks target. Contrast descriptive, not causal isolation of movement.
